# DREAM Lab (UIUC)

> DREAM Lab (Developing Reliable and Efficient AI for Medicine) is Haohan Wang's research lab at the School of Information Sciences, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. The lab builds reliable agentic AI for scientific discovery, studies the security of AI agents, and develops AI methods for computational biology.

Research areas:
- Agentic AI for scientific discovery: LLM agents and multi-agent systems that analyze biological data and do scientific reasoning, e.g. GenoTEX (benchmark for gene expression analysis agents), GenoMAS (multi-agent gene expression analysis, ACL Findings 2026), SCTA (target gene discovery from single-cell RNA-seq), and agentic transcriptomic and proteomic discovery.
- Multi-agent LLM systems and their reliability: agent primitives, agent communication, test-time scaling, self-evolving agents.
- Security of AI agents: prompt injection (SecFid, ICML 2026 Spotlight), jailbreaks, guardrails, and visibility in LLM-based search (CORE).
- AI for computational biology: genetics of complex traits such as Alzheimer's disease and cancer.

Haohan Wang is an Assistant Professor in the School of Information Sciences, affiliated with the Beckman Institute and the Siebel School of Computing and Data Science. He gives invited talks, seminars, and tutorials on agentic AI for scientific discovery and on LLM security; his homepage lists past talks and contact details.

## Project pages
- [SecFid](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/secfid/): benchmark for security and fidelity of prompt injection defenses (ICML 2026 Spotlight)

## Blog posts
- [Can AI Agents Analyze Gene Expression Data Like Experts?](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/ai_agents_gene_expression_analysis.html) (2026-10-16): Can AI agents analyze gene expression data? GenoMAS (ACL Findings 2026) reaches 60.48% F1 on GenoTEX, up from 43.63%; human experts score 71.63%.
- [How Should an AI Theorem Prover Pick a Proof Method?](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/ai_theorem_prover_proof_method_selection.html) (2026-10-15): How should an AI theorem prover pick a proof method? Letting each method propose its own use put a correct one in the top 5 for 95.0% of Putnam problems.
- [Does Recursive Self-Improvement Make AI Agents Forget?](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/recursive_self_improvement_agents_forget.html) (2026-10-14): Does recursive self-improvement make AI agents forget? Often, yes. Preserving old capabilities lifted retained task success from 41.8% to 52.8% in one test.
- [Is AI Math Just Search? What LLMs Miss Between Math Fields](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/ai_math_just_search_hidden_hypotheses.html) (2026-10-12): Is AI math just search? When 7 LLMs restated theorems in a more general field, 60.6% of rewrites silently widened the claim, an error no checker sees.
- [Vision Transformer Robustness: The Inputs a ViT Cannot See](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/vision_transformer_robustness_nullspace.html) (2026-10-09): Vision transformer robustness: ViT-S/32 cannot see 2,688 of 3,072 input dimensions per patch, and nullspace fine-tuning lifts ViT-S's average from 26.5 to 34.5.
- [Can Aligned LLMs Jailbreak Themselves? Inside the SLIP Attack](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/aligned_llms_jailbreak_themselves.html) (2026-10-07): Yes. In our COLM 2026 paper, aligned LLMs jailbreak themselves via SLIP: 94.7% average attack success on AdvBench across 11 models, with about 7.9 queries.
- [RAG That Learns Over Time: Source Learning for LLM Agents](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/rag_that_learns_over_time.html) (2026-10-05): SourceLearn builds RAG that learns over time: a persistent source model beat Hybrid RAG by up to 22.6 points, best in 13 of 15 settings.
- [Agent Primitives: Reusable Latent Building Blocks for Multi-Agent Systems](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/agent_primitives.html) (2026-07-10): Agent Primitives (ICML 2026): reusable latent building blocks for LLM multi-agent systems, composed by an Organizer and connected via KV-cache communication.
- [The Hidden Cost of Prompt Injection Defense](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/security_fidelity_tradeoff.html) (2026-07-09): Prompt injection defenses are scored on attack success, which hides lost content. SecFid (ICML 2026 Spotlight) measures both security and fidelity.
- [How to Test Whether Your Product Descriptions Influence AI Shopping Recommendations](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/test_product_descriptions_ai_recommendations.html) (2026-06-13): A step-by-step protocol for testing whether product descriptions change AI shopping recommendations, using the CORE method and ProductBench.
- [CORE: Controlling Output Rankings in Generative Engines for LLM-based Search](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/controlling_output_rankings_core.html) (2026-06-13): Project page for CORE: controlling output rankings in generative engines for LLM-based search, with the ProductBench benchmark and results on four LLMs.
- [CORE Explained: How to Improve Visibility in LLM-Based Search (Step by Step)](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/core_explained.html) (2026-06-13): A step-by-step explainer of CORE, our method for studying how retrieved content changes rankings in LLM-based search, with definitions and FAQ.
- [SEO vs GEO vs CORE: Techniques for Visibility in LLM-Based Search](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/comparing_llm_search_visibility.html) (2026-06-13): A comparison of SEO, generative engine optimization (GEO), and our CORE method for how content is ranked in LLM-based search, written by the CORE authors.
- [When More Reasoning is Actually Less: The Science Behind Optimal Thinking in LLMs](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/when_more_reasoning_is_actually_less.html) (2025-12-01): Why more chain-of-thought can hurt LLM accuracy: the inverted U-curve, three failure modes of reasoning, and the case for adaptive reasoning.
- [From Parameter Learning to Prompt Learning: The Evolution of Prompt Optimization](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/evolution_of_prompt_optimization.html) (2025-11-01): How prompt optimization mirrors the history of neural network training, from perturbation methods to gradient-based techniques, and what may come next.
- [1000 Ideas for Your Next Trustworthy Machine Learning Paper](https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/blogs/thousand_ideas_trustworthy_ML.html) (2023-10-01): Three universal frameworks for generating trustworthy ML research ideas across robustness, adversarial security, interpretability, and fairness.
